about: Recipe packs served to the app at GET /v1/content/recipes, so new recipes arrive without an app update. Each pack has an id, a title, and recipes in the same shape as the app's ios/RefrigeratorRecipes/Resources/SampleRecipes.json, each with its own unique 'id' slug (never reuse a library id or title). Tags and cuisines must come from FridgeCore's RecipeTag and Cuisine lists. Lint before pushing: python3 ios/tools/recipe_lint.py ios/RefrigeratorRecipes/Resources/SampleRecipes.json server/content/recipe-packs.json. See server/README.md.

recipes.title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
recipes.summary: Chicken thighs soaked in a blended Scotch bonnet, allspice, thyme and scallion marinade, then grilled or roasted until charred. Hot; use one seeded pepper for milder.

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet peppers
ingredients.note: find it at Caribbean or Latin grocers and many supermarkets; or use a habanero; seed one or both for less heat

instructions: Put the green onions, Scotch bonnets, garlic, ginger, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, brown sugar, soy sauce, lime juice, oil, salt and pepper in a blender and blitz to a thick, fairly smooth paste. Wear gloves or wash your hands well after handling the peppers.
Cut 2 or 3 deep slashes in each chicken thigh, put them in a bowl or zip-top bag and rub the marinade all over and into the cuts. Refrigerate at least 1 hour, or overnight for the best flavor.

To grill, heat a grill to medium and oil the grates. Cook the chicken skin side up over indirect heat with the lid closed for about 30 minutes, then move it over the coals and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side until charred in spots.
To roast instead, heat the oven to 425°F and bake the chicken skin side up on a foil-lined sheet pan for 35 to 40 minutes, then broil 2 to 3 minutes until the edges blacken.
Check that the chicken reads at least 175°F near the bone, rest it 5 minutes and serve with rice and peas and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
recipes.summary: Rice simmered with red kidney beans, coconut milk, thyme, scallion and allspice until fluffy and gently savory. The whole Scotch bonnet adds aroma, not heat, as long as it doesn't burst.

ingredients.name: long-grain rice
ingredients.note: rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: find it at Caribbean or Latin grocers and many supermarkets; or use a habanero; keep it whole

instructions: Put the coconut milk, water, kidney beans, green onions, garlic, thyme, allspice and salt in a heavy pot with a tight lid and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Stir in the rinsed rice and lay the whole Scotch bonnet on top, if using. Return to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Check that the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender; if it's still firm, sprinkle in 2 tbsp water, cover and cook 5 minutes more.
Turn off the heat and let it sit covered for 5 minutes. Carefully lift out the pepper, green onions and thyme stems, then fluff the rice with a fork and serve.

recipes.title: Ropa Vieja (Cuban Shredded Beef)
recipes.summary: Flank steak braised slowly with peppers, onion, tomato, cumin and oregano until it pulls into tender shreds in a rich, mild sauce. Lovely over rice with black beans.

ingredients.name: flank steak
ingredients.note: cut into 3 or 4 pieces; or beef chuck

instructions: Pat the beef dry and season with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the beef 3 to 4 minutes per side until well colored, then set it on a plate.

Lower the heat to medium, add the onion and both peppers and cook 6 to 8 minutes, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, until softened. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, cumin and oregano and cook 1 minute until the paste darkens.

Add the crushed tomatoes, broth and bay leaves, return the beef and any juices, and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low for 2 hours, turning the beef once, until it falls apart easily when prodded with a fork.
Lift out the beef and shred it with two forks along the grain. Discard the bay leaves.
Return the beef to the pot with the olives and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, until the sauce clings to the meat. Taste for salt, sprinkle with cilantro and serve with white rice and black beans.
Slow-cooker option: after step 2, put everything except the olives in a slow cooker and cook on low for 8 hours, then shred and finish as above.

recipes.title: Trinidadian Curry Chicken
recipes.summary: Chicken marinated in fresh herb green seasoning, then cooked in toasted curry powder with potatoes until the gravy turns thick and golden. Medium heat; leave out the Scotch bonnet seeds for milder.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.note: bone-in, skin removed, cut in half through the bone if large

ingredients.name: curry powder
ingredients.note: Caribbean-style if you can find it; any mild Madras curry powder works

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: find it at Caribbean or Latin grocers and many supermarkets; or use a habanero

instructions: Blend the cilantro, green onions, garlic, thyme, lime juice and 2 tbsp water to a coarse green paste. Toss the chicken with half of it, 1 tbsp of the curry powder and 1 tsp salt, and marinate 20 minutes or up to overnight in the fridge.
Mix the remaining 2 tbsp curry powder and the cumin with 1/4 cup water to a loose paste.

Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 4 minutes until soft, then add the curry paste and stir constantly for 3 to 4 minutes until it darkens slightly, smells toasty and the oil starts to separate.
Add the chicken and stir to coat it in the curry. Cook 5 minutes, turning, until the outside is sealed and coated.
Add the potatoes, the rest of the green seasoning, the Scotch bonnet and the hot water. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on medium-low for 25 minutes.

Uncover and simmer 8 to 10 minutes more, stirring now and then, until the potatoes start to break down and thicken the gravy and the chicken reaches 175°F. Season with the remaining salt, remove the pepper and serve with rice or roti.

recipes.title: Cuban Black Bean Soup
recipes.summary: A thick, smoky-savory black bean soup with green pepper, cumin, oregano and a splash of vinegar to brighten it, made fast with canned beans.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and green pepper with a pinch of salt and cook 6 to 7 minutes, stirring, until soft and starting to brown at the edges.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and oregano and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beans, broth and bay leaves, bring to a boil, then simmer 12 minutes so the flavors meld.
Remove the bay leaves. Blend about half the soup with an immersion blender, or blend 2 cups in a blender and stir it back in, so the soup is thick but still has whole beans.
Stir in the vinegar, taste for salt and serve topped with chopped red onion and cilantro, with rice on the side if you like.

recipes.title: Cubano (Cuban Pressed Sandwich)
recipes.summary: Roast pork, ham, Swiss cheese, pickles and yellow mustard pressed in buttered bread until crisp outside and melty inside. A great use for leftover pork.

ingredients.name: bread
ingredients.note: 1 Cuban loaf or 4 soft hoagie rolls, split

ingredients.name: roast pork
ingredients.note: thinly sliced; leftover pork roast or deli roast pork

instructions: If using one long loaf, cut it into 4 pieces and split each one. Spread the cut sides thinly with mustard.
Layer the bottoms with half the cheese, then the ham, roast pork, pickles and the remaining cheese, and close the sandwiches. Spread the outsides with the butter.
Heat a large skillet or griddle over medium heat. Add the sandwiches and press them down hard with a second heavy skillet (or a foil-wrapped brick).
Cook 4 to 5 minutes per side, pressing again after flipping, until the bread is flat, crisp and golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut each sandwich on the diagonal and serve hot.

recipes.title: Jamaican Escovitch Fish
recipes.summary: Crisp pan-fried white fish under a tangy, warm pickle of onion, carrot, peppers and allspice. Hot from the Scotch bonnet; use a jalapeño for milder.

ingredients.name: white fish fillets
ingredients.note: snapper, tilapia or cod, about 4 fillets

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: find it at Caribbean or Latin grocers and many supermarkets; or use a habanero; or a jalapeño for milder, thinly sliced

instructions: Make the pickle: in a small saucepan bring the vinegar, water, sugar, allspice and 1/2 tsp salt to a simmer. Add the onion, carrot, bell pepper and Scotch bonnet and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until just wilted but still a little crunchy, then turn off the heat.
Pat the fish very dry and season with the remaining 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Dust both sides lightly with cornstarch and shake off the excess.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Fry the fish 3 to 4 minutes per side, without moving it, until golden and crisp and the flesh flakes easily.

Lay the fish on a platter and spoon the warm vegetables and some of the pickling liquid over the top. Serve right away, or let it sit 15 minutes to soak up the flavors; it's traditionally eaten with festival or bread.

recipes.title: Habichuelas Guisadas (Puerto Rican Stewed Beans)
recipes.summary: Pink beans simmered with a quick cilantro-pepper sofrito, tomato sauce, potato and olives into a saucy, savory stew. Spoon over white rice.

ingredients.name: pink beans
ingredients.note: 15 oz each, drained and rinsed; or pinto beans

ingredients.name: paprika
ingredients.note: stands in for the achiote in sazón

ingredients.name: potato
ingredients.note: medium, peeled and cut in 1/2-inch cubes; or 1 cup butternut squash

instructions: Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Add the onion, green pepper, garlic and half the cilantro and cook 5 minutes, stirring, until soft and fragrant; this is your sofrito.
Stir in the tomato sauce, paprika, cumin and oregano and let it bubble 2 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the beans, potato, broth, olives and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered for 20 to 25 minutes until the potato is tender.
Mash a few beans and potato cubes against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce. Taste for salt, stir in the rest of the cilantro and serve over rice.

recipes.title: Smothered Pork Chops
recipes.summary: Seared pork chops simmered in a peppery onion gravy until fork-tender. Soul-food comfort that's lovely with rice or mashed potatoes and greens.
instructions: Mix the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Season the chops all over with half the mix, then dredge them lightly in 3 tbsp of the flour.
Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chops 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden, then move them to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the butter and onions with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt, and cook 8 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until soft and golden. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Sprinkle in the remaining flour and the rest of the spice mix and stir 2 minutes. Slowly whisk in the broth, add the thyme and simmer until it thickens into a gravy, about 2 minutes.
Nestle the chops back into the gravy with any juices, cover and simmer on low for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until the pork is tender and reads at least 145°F.
Thin the gravy with a splash of broth or water if it gets too thick, sprinkle with parsley and serve over rice or mashed potatoes.

recipes.title: Oven-Fried Chicken
recipes.summary: Buttermilk-soaked drumsticks and thighs in a seasoned flour crust, baked hot until crunchy and juicy with no pot of oil. Mild enough for kids.
instructions: Whisk the buttermilk, hot sauce and 1 tsp salt in a bowl, add the chicken and turn to coat. Soak at least 15 minutes, or cover and refrigerate up to overnight.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Pour the melted butter and oil onto a rimmed baking sheet and tilt it to coat, or set a wire rack on the sheet and brush it with the fat.
In a shallow dish mix the flour, cornstarch, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, pepper and the remaining 1 tsp salt.

Lift each piece of chicken from the buttermilk, let the excess drip off, and press firmly into the flour to coat all over. Set on the baking sheet skin side down, leaving space between pieces, and let sit 5 minutes so the coating sets.
Bake 25 minutes, then flip with a thin spatula and bake 20 minutes more, until the crust is deep golden and crisp and the chicken reads 175°F near the bone.
Rest 5 minutes on a rack so the bottoms stay crunchy, then serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Southern Chicken and Dumplings
recipes.summary: Tender chicken and vegetables in a creamy, thyme-scented broth topped with fluffy drop dumplings that steam right in the pot. Gentle and filling.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: divided; 3 tbsp kept cold for the dumplings

instructions: Melt 2 tbsp butter in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic for 1 minute.

Sprinkle in 1/4 cup flour and stir 2 minutes. Slowly whisk in the broth, then add the whole chicken thighs, thyme, bay leaf, 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.

While it simmers, make the dumpling dough: whisk the remaining 2 cups flour, baking powder and 1 tsp salt, then rub in the 3 tbsp cold butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs. Stir in the milk just until a soft, shaggy dough forms.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot. Discard the bay leaf and bring the stew back to a gentle simmer; it should be slightly thick.
Drop heaping tablespoons of dough over the surface, cover tightly and simmer on low for 15 minutes without lifting the lid, until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through in the middle.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve in bowls.

recipes.title: Cornmeal-Crusted Catfish
recipes.summary: Catfish fillets brushed with mustard, coated in seasoned cornmeal and pan-fried in a little oil until crunchy. A fast, classic Southern fish supper.
instructions: Pat the fish very dry and brush both sides thinly with the mustard.
Mix the cornmeal, paprika, garlic powder, cayenne, salt and pepper on a plate. Press each fillet into the mixture to coat both sides well.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until a pinch of cornmeal sizzles right away.
Fry the fillets 4 to 5 minutes per side, without moving them, until the crust is deep golden and the fish flakes easily in the thickest part. Work in batches if needed so the pan isn't crowded.
Drain briefly on a paper towel–lined plate and serve hot with lemon wedges and hot sauce, with slaw or collards on the side.

recipes.title: Weeknight Hoppin' John
recipes.summary: Black-eyed peas simmered with bacon, onion, celery and green pepper, then folded with rice. A New Year's Day tradition that's good any night.
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large skillet or pot over medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes until crisp. Spoon off all but about 2 tbsp of the fat.
Add the onion, celery and green pepper and cook 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic, thyme and pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the black-eyed peas and broth, bring to a simmer and cook 6 to 8 minutes, until slightly thickened and some peas start to break down.
Fold in the rice and cook 2 to 3 minutes, stirring gently, until hot and the liquid is mostly absorbed. Season with salt, then top with green onions and pass the hot sauce.

recipes.title: Southern Collard Greens with Smoked Turkey
recipes.summary: Collards braised low and slow with smoked turkey, onion and a splash of vinegar until silky, with plenty of savory pot likker to sop up with cornbread.

ingredients.name: collard greens
ingredients.note: 2 large bunches, stems removed, leaves sliced into ribbons and washed well

ingredients.name: smoked turkey wing
ingredients.note: or smoked turkey neck or leg; find it near the ham

instructions: Put the smoked turkey and broth in a large pot, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 30 minutes to build a smoky broth.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute. Add this to the pot.
Add the collards a few handfuls at a time, stirring each batch down as it wilts. Stir in the vinegar, brown sugar and pepper flakes.
Cover and simmer on low for 45 to 50 minutes, stirring now and then, until the greens are silky and tender. Add a splash of water if the liquid drops below the greens.
Lift out the turkey, pull the meat off the bones, chop it and return it to the pot. Season with salt and pepper and serve with the pot likker and hot sauce.

recipes.title: Southern Skillet Cornbread
recipes.summary: Golden, crisp-edged buttermilk cornbread baked in a sizzling cast-iron skillet. Barely sweet, the way it's served alongside greens, beans and chili.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: optional; leave out for a savory cornbread

instructions: Put the butter in a 10-inch cast-iron skillet and set it in the oven while it heats to 425°F, about 10 minutes, until the butter is melted and foaming.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a bowl. In another bowl whisk the buttermilk and eggs.
Carefully take out the hot skillet, swirl the butter to coat the sides, and pour most of it into the buttermilk mixture. Stir the wet ingredients into the dry just until no dry streaks remain.
Pour the batter into the hot skillet; it should sizzle. Bake 20 to 22 minutes until the top is golden and a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool 5 minutes, then cut into wedges and serve warm.

recipes.title: Southern Peach Cobbler
recipes.summary: Juicy cinnamon peaches baked under a buttery batter that rises up golden and crisp around the fruit. Use fresh peaches in summer or frozen any time.

ingredients.name: peaches
ingredients.note: about 6 fresh, peeled and sliced; or frozen sliced peaches, thawed

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. In a saucepan, combine the peaches, 1/4 cup sugar, the cinnamon and lemon juice and simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes until juicy, then stir in the vanilla.
Put the butter in a 9x13-inch baking dish and set it in the oven for 5 minutes until melted.
Whisk the flour, remaining 1 cup sugar, baking powder and salt, then whisk in the milk until smooth.
Pour the batter evenly over the melted butter and don't stir. Spoon the peaches and their juices over the top, again without stirring.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes until the batter has risen around the fruit and is deep golden and crisp at the edges.
Cool at least 15 minutes so the juices thicken, then serve warm, with vanilla ice cream if you like.

recipes.title: Ca Kho (Vietnamese Caramel-Braised Fish)
recipes.summary: Catfish simmered in a dark, bittersweet caramel with fish sauce, shallots and lots of black pepper until glossy and sticky. Made to be eaten with plenty of rice.

ingredients.name: fish fillets
ingredients.note: catfish is traditional; cod or tilapia also work; cut into 2-inch pieces

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.note: find it in the Asian aisle of most supermarkets

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: or coconut water for a rounder, sweeter sauce

instructions: Pat the fish dry and set it aside while you make the caramel.

Put the sugar and 1 tbsp of the water in a medium heavy pot or deep skillet over medium heat. Cook without stirring, swirling the pan now and then, until the syrup turns the color of dark amber and smells toasty, 4 to 6 minutes.

Take the pan off the heat and carefully add the oil, shallots and garlic; the caramel will hiss and seize. Return to low heat and stir for 1 minute until the shallots soften and the caramel melts back into a sauce.
Stir in the fish sauce, the rest of the water and the black pepper and bring to a simmer. Add the fish in a single layer and spoon the sauce over it.
Cover and simmer gently for 12 minutes, turning the pieces once with a spatula so they don't break.

Uncover and simmer 8 to 10 minutes more, basting often, until the sauce is thick, dark and clings to the fish. Scatter over the green onions and chili and cook 1 minute more. Serve with steamed rice and a simple vegetable or cucumber slices.

recipes.title: Goi Ga (Vietnamese Chicken and Cabbage Salad)
recipes.summary: Poached chicken tossed with crunchy cabbage, carrots, herbs and a sweet-sour lime and fish sauce dressing, then topped with peanuts. Mildly spicy; leave out the jalapeño for no heat.

ingredients.name: cabbage
ingredients.note: very thinly sliced; green, napa or a mix

ingredients.name: red onion
ingredients.note: very thinly sliced and soaked in cold water 10 minutes

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.note: find it in the Asian aisle of most supermarkets

ingredients.name: mint
ingredients.note: leaves, torn; Vietnamese coriander (rau răm) is traditional if you can find it

instructions: Put the chicken in a saucepan, cover with cold water by an inch and add a big pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover, turn off the heat and let it sit 12 to 15 minutes until the thickest part reaches 165°F.
Meanwhile, whisk the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, garlic and jalapeño with 2 tbsp water until the sugar dissolves. Taste: it should be salty, sour and sweet in balance.
Lift the chicken out, let it cool for a few minutes, then shred it into thin strips with two forks.
In a large bowl, toss the cabbage, carrots and drained onion with about two thirds of the dressing and let it sit 5 minutes to soften slightly.
Add the chicken, mint and cilantro and toss with the remaining dressing. Pile onto a platter and scatter with peanuts just before serving.

recipes.title: Lemongrass Tofu Banh Mi
recipes.summary: Crisp lemongrass-and-garlic tofu stuffed into crusty rolls with quick-pickled carrots, cucumber, cilantro and a swipe of mayo. Use the jalapeño to taste.

ingredients.name: tofu
ingredients.note: extra-firm, pressed and cut into ½-inch-thick slabs

ingredients.name: lemongrass
ingredients.note: tender inner part finely minced; or 2 tbsp lemongrass paste from the produce section

ingredients.name: french bread
ingredients.note: 4 soft, crusty 6-inch rolls or 1 long baguette cut into 4

instructions: Stir the rice vinegar, sugar and salt with ¼ cup warm water until dissolved. Add the carrots and set aside to pickle for at least 20 minutes.
Mix the lemongrass, soy sauce, brown sugar and garlic in a shallow dish. Add the tofu slabs, turn to coat and leave for 10 minutes.

Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Lay in the tofu (save any leftover marinade) and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side until deeply golden and crisp at the edges. Pour in the leftover marinade for the last 30 seconds and turn the tofu to glaze it.
Warm the rolls in a 400°F oven for 4 to 5 minutes until the crust crackles, then split them, leaving one side hinged.
Stir the sriracha into the mayonnaise if using and spread it inside the rolls. Fill with tofu, drained pickled carrots, cucumber, cilantro and jalapeño, and serve right away.

recipes.title: Bo Luc Lac (Vietnamese Shaking Beef)
recipes.summary: Cubes of sirloin seared hard in a smoking-hot pan and 'shaken' with garlic, oyster sauce and butter, served over peppery greens, tomato and onion with a lime-pepper dip.

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.note: find it in the Asian aisle of most supermarkets

ingredients.name: red onion
ingredients.note: half cut into thick wedges, half thinly sliced

ingredients.name: mixed greens
ingredients.note: watercress is traditional; arugula or baby spinach also work

instructions: Toss the beef with half the garlic, the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar and black pepper. Let it sit 10 minutes while you prepare everything else.

Toss the sliced onion with 1 tsp of the lime juice and arrange the greens, tomatoes and sliced onion on a platter. For the dip, mix the remaining lime juice with ½ tsp salt and ½ tsp black pepper in a tiny bowl.

Heat a large cast-iron or heavy skillet over high heat until it smokes. Add 1 tbsp oil and half the beef in a single layer; leave it untouched for 1 minute until a dark crust forms, then shake the pan to turn the cubes and sear 1 to 2 minutes more for medium-rare. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining oil and beef.
Return all the beef to the pan with the onion wedges, the remaining garlic and the butter. Shake and toss for 1 minute until the butter foams and the onions just soften.
Tip the beef and pan juices over the greens and serve at once with the lime-pepper dip and steamed rice.

recipes.title: Goi Cuon Chay (Tofu Summer Rolls with Peanut-Hoisin Sauce)
recipes.summary: Fresh rice paper rolls packed with golden tofu, rice noodles, crisp vegetables and herbs, served with a creamy peanut-hoisin dipping sauce. A fun roll-your-own dinner.

ingredients.name: tofu
ingredients.note: extra-firm, patted dry and cut into thin sticks

ingredients.name: rice paper
ingredients.note: 8½-inch round wrappers; in the Asian aisle

ingredients.name: lettuce
ingredients.note: soft leaves such as green leaf or butter lettuce, torn

ingredients.name: basil
ingredients.note: leaves; Thai basil if you can find it

instructions: Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and fry the tofu sticks, turning, until golden on most sides, 8 to 10 minutes. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt and let cool.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package, usually 3 to 4 minutes, then rinse under cold water and drain well.
Whisk the hoisin, peanut butter, lime juice, garlic and sriracha with 3 to 4 tbsp warm water until smooth and pourable. Top with chopped peanuts.
Fill a wide shallow dish with warm water. Dip one rice paper for 2 to 3 seconds until just pliable but not floppy and lay it on a damp board; it will keep softening as you fill it.

Across the lower third, lay a few herb leaves, then lettuce, a small bundle of noodles, cucumber, carrot and 2 or 3 tofu sticks. Fold the bottom up over the filling, fold in the sides and roll up snugly.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers, keeping finished rolls apart under a damp towel so they don't stick. Serve within an hour with the dipping sauce.

recipes.title: Canh Chua Tom (Vietnamese Sweet and Sour Shrimp Soup)
recipes.summary: A bright, tangy tamarind broth with shrimp, pineapple, tomatoes and bean sprouts, finished with lots of fresh herbs. Light but satisfying with rice; mildly spicy if you add the chili.

ingredients.name: tamarind paste
ingredients.note: seedless concentrate; find it at Asian or Latin grocers; or use 3 tbsp lime juice added at the end

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.note: find it in the Asian aisle of most supermarkets

ingredients.name: pineapple
ingredients.note: fresh or canned chunks, cut bite-size

ingredients.name: celery
ingredients.note: sliced on an angle; stands in for bạc hà (taro stem)

ingredients.name: cilantro
ingredients.note: chopped; rice paddy herb (ngò om) is traditional if you can find it

ingredients.name: basil
ingredients.note: leaves; Thai basil if you can find it

instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the garlic for 1 minute until golden and fragrant.
Add the water and tamarind paste, whisking to dissolve the tamarind, and bring to a boil. Stir in the fish sauce and sugar.
Add the pineapple, tomatoes and celery and simmer 5 to 6 minutes until the tomatoes begin to soften and the celery is just tender-crisp.
Taste the broth: it should be clearly sour, a little sweet and salty. Adjust with more tamarind, sugar or fish sauce.
Add the shrimp and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until pink and curled. Turn off the heat and stir in the bean sprouts.
Ladle into bowls, top with cilantro, basil and chili and serve with steamed rice on the side.

recipes.title: San Bei Ji (Taiwanese Three-Cup Chicken)
recipes.summary: Chicken thighs cooked down with toasted sesame oil, soy sauce and rice wine with heaps of garlic and ginger until sticky, then tossed with a big handful of basil.

ingredients.name: ginger
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into thin coins

ingredients.name: shaoxing wine
ingredients.note: Taiwanese rice wine (mi jiu) is traditional; or dry sherry; find Shaoxing wine at Asian grocers

ingredients.name: basil
ingredients.note: leaves; Thai basil is closest to Taiwanese basil

instructions: Heat the sesame oil in a large wok or heavy skillet over medium heat. Add the ginger and cook 3 to 4 minutes until the edges curl and turn golden, then add the garlic and cook 2 minutes more until lightly browned.
Raise the heat to medium-high, add the chicken and the white parts of the green onions and stir-fry 5 minutes until the chicken is lightly browned all over.
Pour in the rice wine and let it bubble for 1 minute, then add the soy sauce, sugar and pepper flakes.
Cover and simmer over medium-low for 8 minutes, then uncover and cook over medium-high, stirring often, until the sauce reduces to a dark, sticky glaze that coats the chicken, 4 to 6 minutes.
Turn off the heat, add the basil and green onion tops and toss until wilted. Serve straight from the pan with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Lu Rou Fan (Taiwanese Braised Pork Rice)
recipes.summary: Finely chopped pork belly braised low and slow with soy, shallots and five-spice until meltingly tender, spooned over rice with soy-stained eggs. Taiwan's favorite comfort bowl.

ingredients.name: pork belly
ingredients.note: skin-on or skinless; freeze 20 minutes, then cut into ¼-inch pieces

ingredients.name: shallots
ingredients.note: thinly sliced; or ½ cup store-bought fried shallots

ingredients.name: shaoxing wine
ingredients.note: or dry sherry; find Shaoxing wine at Asian grocers

ingredients.name: five-spice powder
ingredients.note: in the spice aisle of most supermarkets or at Asian grocers

ingredients.name: rice
ingredients.note: uncooked jasmine or medium-grain, cooked to serve

ingredients.name: pickled mustard greens
ingredients.note: chopped, to serve; at Asian grocers

instructions: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat and fry the shallots, stirring often, until deep golden and crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Scoop out half for garnish.

Raise the heat to medium-high, add the pork and cook, stirring, until the fat renders and the pork loses its pink color and starts to brown in spots, 8 to 10 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Pour in the rice wine and let it bubble for 30 seconds, then stir in the soy sauce, brown sugar, five-spice, white pepper and water. Bring to a boil.
Nestle in the peeled eggs, cover and simmer on low for 1 hour, stirring and turning the eggs every 15 minutes, until the pork is very tender and the sauce is glossy. Meanwhile, cook the rice.
If the sauce is thin, simmer uncovered 5 minutes more. Skim off some of the fat if you like.

Spoon the pork and plenty of sauce over bowls of rice, add a halved egg and the reserved crispy shallots, and serve with blanched bok choy and pickled greens. The pork (without the eggs) keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

recipes.title: Hong Shao Niu Rou Mian (Taiwanese Braised Beef Noodle Soup)
recipes.summary: Beef chuck braised in a dark, spiced broth with chili bean paste, tomato and star anise, served over chewy noodles with bok choy. Medium heat; halve the bean paste for milder.

ingredients.name: beef chuck
ingredients.note: or boneless shank, cut into 1½-inch chunks

ingredients.name: green onions
ingredients.note: white parts in 2-inch lengths, tops sliced for garnish

ingredients.name: doubanjiang
ingredients.note: spicy chili bean paste; find it at Asian grocers or online; or use 1 tbsp chili garlic sauce plus 1 tbsp miso

ingredients.name: shaoxing wine
ingredients.note: or dry sherry; find Shaoxing wine at Asian grocers

ingredients.name: noodles
ingredients.note: fresh or dried wheat noodles, medium-thick

instructions: Put the beef in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil and boil 3 minutes to release the scum. Drain and rinse the beef.

Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Cook the onion, ginger, garlic and green onion whites for 4 minutes until lightly browned, then add the doubanjiang and tomato paste and stir 1 minute until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Add the beef and tomatoes and stir to coat, then pour in the rice wine and let it bubble for 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce, brown sugar, star anise, cinnamon, broth and water. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 2 to 2½ hours until the beef is fork-tender.
Fish out the star anise, cinnamon and ginger slices. Taste the broth and adjust with soy sauce or a splash of water; skim off excess fat.
Near serving time, cook the noodles in a separate pot of boiling water according to the package, adding the bok choy for the last 2 minutes. Drain.
Divide the noodles and bok choy among deep bowls, ladle over the beef and broth and scatter with green onion tops. The braise (without noodles) freezes well for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Cong You Bing (Taiwanese Scallion Pancakes)
recipes.summary: Flaky, chewy pan-fried flatbreads swirled with green onions and sesame oil, crisp outside and layered inside, with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce. Great as a snack or alongside soup.
instructions: Put the flour in a bowl and pour in the hot water while stirring with chopsticks until shaggy. When cool enough to handle, knead 3 to 4 minutes until smooth, adding a spoonful of cold water if dry. Cover and rest 20 minutes.
Mix the sesame oil with 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil and 2 tbsp flour into a loose paste.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces. Roll one into a thin 8-inch round, brush with the oil paste, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and a quarter of the green onions.
Roll the round up tightly like a cigar, then coil the rope into a snail shape and tuck the end underneath. Rest 5 minutes, then gently roll it out again to a 7-inch pancake. Repeat with the rest.

Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a nonstick or cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Cook one pancake 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp, then use two spatulas to scrunch it gently toward the center to separate the flaky layers.

Repeat with the remaining oil and pancakes. Stir the soy sauce, vinegar and chili oil together and serve with the pancakes cut into wedges. Uncooked coiled pancakes freeze well between parchment; cook from frozen a little longer.

recipes.title: Baked Yan Su Ji (Taiwanese Popcorn Chicken)
recipes.summary: Night-market-style popcorn chicken marinated in soy, garlic and five-spice, coated in starch and baked until craggy and crisp, then tossed with crispy basil and pepper salt.

ingredients.name: five-spice powder
ingredients.note: divided; in the spice aisle of most supermarkets or at Asian grocers

ingredients.name: cornstarch
ingredients.note: Taiwanese sweet potato starch gives the classic craggy crust; find it at Asian grocers

ingredients.name: basil
ingredients.note: leaves, patted very dry; Thai basil if you can find it

instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the upper third. Set a wire rack on a foil-lined sheet pan and grease it well.
Toss the chicken with the soy sauce, garlic, ginger, ½ tsp of the five-spice and the sugar. Marinate 10 minutes, then stir in the beaten egg.
Put the cornstarch in a wide bowl. Working in batches, toss the chicken in it, pressing so it sticks and forms craggy bits, then let it sit 2 minutes until the coating looks damp.
Spread the chicken on the rack without touching, drizzle or brush with the oil, and spray any dry, white patches.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges and cooked through. Scatter the basil over the chicken and bake 2 minutes more until the leaves turn crisp and translucent.
Mix the salt, white pepper, remaining five-spice and chili powder. Toss the hot chicken and basil with about half of it, adding more to taste, and serve right away.

recipes.title: Fan Qie Chao Dan (Taiwanese Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry)
recipes.summary: Soft, fluffy scrambled eggs folded into juicy tomatoes cooked down into a sweet-savory sauce. A 15-minute home-style classic that's perfect over rice.

ingredients.name: ketchup
ingredients.note: a common Taiwanese home-style addition for color and tang

instructions: Beat the eggs with ¼ tsp salt and 1 tbsp of the water until smooth and a little frothy.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Pour in the eggs, let them puff for 5 seconds, then push them gently with a spatula into large, soft curds. Remove while still a little runny, after about 1 minute.
Add the remaining oil and the green onion whites and cook 30 seconds. Add the tomatoes and cook, stirring, 3 to 4 minutes until they soften and release their juice.
Stir in the sugar, ketchup, remaining salt and remaining water and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until the juices turn into a light, glossy sauce.
Return the eggs to the pan and fold gently for 30 seconds until just set. Finish with the green onion tops and sesame oil and serve over rice.

recipes.title: Chicken Tinola (Filipino Ginger Chicken Soup)
recipes.summary: A clear, gingery chicken soup with tender chayote and spinach, seasoned simply with fish sauce. Gentle, comforting and quick enough for a weeknight.

ingredients.name: ginger
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into thin matchsticks

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.note: patis; find it in the Asian aisle of most supermarkets

ingredients.name: chayote
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into wedges; or 1 small green papaya, or 2 zucchini added in the last 5 minutes

ingredients.name: baby spinach
ingredients.note: malunggay (moringa) or chili leaves are traditional

instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the ginger, garlic and onion for 3 to 4 minutes until the onion is soft and everything smells fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook, turning, 4 to 5 minutes until the outside turns opaque. Stir in the fish sauce and cook 1 minute more.
Pour in the broth and water and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam. Lower the heat, cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the chayote and simmer 8 to 10 minutes more until it is tender when pierced with a knife and the chicken pulls easily from the bone.
Turn off the heat and stir in the spinach until wilted. Season with pepper and more fish sauce to taste, and serve hot with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Pancit Bihon (Filipino Stir-Fried Rice Noodles)
recipes.summary: Thin rice noodles stir-fried with chicken, cabbage, carrots and green beans in a savory soy and oyster sauce broth, finished with a squeeze of citrus. A party favorite.

ingredients.name: green beans
ingredients.note: or snow peas, trimmed and sliced on an angle

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: cut into wedges; calamansi is traditional

instructions: Soak the rice noodles in warm water for 10 minutes until pliable, then drain. Snip them a few times with scissors so they're easier to toss.
Heat the oil in a large wok or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and garlic 2 minutes until soft, then add the chicken and stir-fry 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through.
Add the carrots, celery and green beans and stir-fry 2 minutes. Add the cabbage and cook 1 minute more until just wilted. Scoop out about half of the vegetables and set aside.
Pour in the broth, soy sauce, oyster sauce and pepper and bring to a boil.
Add the noodles and toss constantly with tongs for 3 to 5 minutes until they absorb nearly all the liquid and turn tender. Fold the reserved vegetables back in.
Pile onto a platter, top with green onions and serve with lemon wedges to squeeze over.

recipes.title: Sinigang na Hipon (Filipino Sour Tamarind Shrimp Soup)
recipes.summary: A tangy tamarind broth loaded with shrimp, tomatoes, radish, green beans and greens. Bright and soothing; the long green chili adds aroma more than heat.

ingredients.name: tamarind paste
ingredients.note: seedless concentrate at Asian or Latin grocers; or 1 packet sinigang soup mix (Knorr or Mama Sita's), found at Asian grocers and many supermarkets

ingredients.name: daikon radish
ingredients.note: sliced into half-moons; or a bunch of red radishes, halved

ingredients.name: green beans
ingredients.note: cut into 2-inch lengths; long beans (sitaw) are traditional

ingredients.name: baby spinach
ingredients.note: or water spinach (kangkong) if you can find it

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.note: find it in the Asian aisle of most supermarkets

instructions: Bring the water, onion and tomatoes to a boil in a large pot. Simmer 8 minutes until the tomatoes soften and start to break down.
Whisk in the tamarind until dissolved and add the radish. Simmer 6 to 8 minutes until the radish is nearly tender and translucent at the edges.
Add the green beans and the whole chilies and simmer 3 minutes until bright green.
Add the shrimp and cook 2 to 3 minutes until just pink and curled. Season with the fish sauce, then taste: it should be boldly sour and savory. Add more tamarind or fish sauce to taste.
Turn off the heat, stir in the spinach until wilted and serve hot with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Baked Lumpiang Shanghai (Filipino Pork Spring Rolls)
recipes.summary: Slim, crunchy spring rolls filled with seasoned ground pork and vegetables, brushed with oil and baked instead of deep-fried. A party staple; freeze extras unbaked.

ingredients.name: lumpia wrappers
ingredients.note: thin spring roll wrappers, thawed; in the freezer section of Asian grocers

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper third. Line two sheet pans with parchment and brush lightly with oil.
Mix the pork, carrot, onion, garlic, green onions, egg, soy sauce, pepper and salt with your hands until evenly combined. Fry a teaspoon in a small pan to check the seasoning if you like.
Peel off one wrapper and keep the rest under a damp towel. Lay it as a diamond and spread a heaping tablespoon of filling into a thin log about 4 inches long near the bottom corner.
Fold the bottom corner over the filling, fold in the sides and roll up tightly, sealing the top corner with a dab of water. Repeat with the remaining filling, then cut each roll in half on an angle.
Arrange the rolls on the pans seam side down and brush all over with oil. Bake 18 to 20 minutes, turning once halfway, until deep golden and crisp and the filling is cooked through (160°F).
Let cool 5 minutes and serve with sweet chili sauce. To freeze, freeze unbaked rolls on a tray, then bag them; bake from frozen for 25 to 28 minutes.

recipes.title: Poulet à la Moutarde (Chicken in Mustard Cream Sauce)
recipes.summary: Golden chicken thighs simmered in a tangy Dijon and cream pan sauce with shallots and thyme. A French bistro classic that comes together on a weeknight.

ingredients.name: shallots
ingredients.note: finely chopped; or half a small onion

instructions: Pat the chicken dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken 5 to 6 minutes per side until deep golden, then move it to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the shallots and cook 2 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the broth and scrape up the browned bits from the pan. Whisk in both mustards, the cream and the thyme.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan, cover and simmer gently 8 to 10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 175°F and the sauce coats a spoon.
Taste the sauce for salt, scatter with parsley and serve with rice, potatoes or crusty bread to mop it up.

recipes.title: Ratatouille (Provençal Summer Vegetable Stew)
recipes.summary: Eggplant, zucchini, peppers and tomatoes slowly stewed in olive oil with garlic and herbs until silky. Even better the next day, warm or at room temperature.
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the eggplant with a pinch of salt and cook 8 minutes, stirring, until browned in spots and softening; scoop it out.
Add another 1 tbsp oil and the zucchini and cook 5 minutes until lightly golden at the edges; scoop it out to join the eggplant.
Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining oil, the onion and peppers and cook 8 minutes until soft and sweet. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, thyme, bay leaf and salt, then return the eggplant and zucchini. Bring to a simmer.
Cover partly and cook on low for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until everything is tender and the juices have thickened.
Remove the bay leaf, season with pepper and more salt, and stir in the basil. Serve warm with bread, over rice or polenta, or beside grilled chicken or eggs.

recipes.title: Croque Monsieur (French Ham and Cheese Toastie)
recipes.summary: The Paris café sandwich: ham and Gruyère on toasted bread, topped with a quick béchamel and more cheese, then broiled until bubbling and golden.

ingredients.name: nutmeg
ingredients.note: freshly grated if you have it

ingredients.name: sandwich bread
ingredients.note: sturdy white or pain de mie

instructions: Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches from the heat, and line a baking sheet with foil.

Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, whisking, until thick enough to coat a spoon. Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Lay 4 slices of bread on the sheet, spread thinly with mustard, then top with the ham and half the cheese. Close with the remaining bread.
Melt the last 1 tbsp butter and brush it over the tops. Broil 1 to 2 minutes until golden, flip carefully, and spread the béchamel over the untoasted sides.
Scatter over the rest of the cheese and broil 2 to 4 minutes, watching closely, until bubbling and browned in spots. Rest 2 minutes, then cut and serve.

recipes.title: Quiche aux Légumes (Spinach, Mushroom and Gruyère Quiche)
recipes.summary: A silky egg custard with sautéed mushrooms, spinach and Gruyère in a store-bought crust. Good warm or at room temperature for brunch, lunch or a light dinner.

ingredients.name: nutmeg
ingredients.note: freshly grated if you have it

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Fit the crust into a 9-inch pie plate, crimp the edge and chill while you make the filling.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms and onion 7 to 8 minutes until the mushrooms are browned and their liquid has cooked off.
Add the spinach a handful at a time and stir until wilted, about 2 minutes. Tip into a sieve and press out as much liquid as you can so the quiche doesn't turn watery.
Whisk the eggs, milk, cream, salt, pepper and nutmeg in a bowl until smooth.
Scatter half the cheese over the crust, then the vegetables, then the rest of the cheese. Pour in the custard.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the edges are puffed and golden and the center wobbles only slightly when you nudge the dish. Cool 15 minutes before slicing so it sets.

recipes.title: Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée (French Onion Soup)
recipes.summary: Onions cooked low and slow until deep brown and sweet, simmered in beef broth, then topped with toasted baguette and melted Gruyère.

ingredients.name: dry white wine
ingredients.note: or 1 tbsp sherry vinegar plus 1/2 cup extra broth

instructions: Melt the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onions and salt, cover and cook 10 minutes, stirring once or twice, until they collapse.

Uncover, stir in the sugar and cook 40 to 45 minutes more, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom, until the onions are soft and a deep caramel brown. If they start to scorch, lower the heat and add a splash of water.
Stir in the garlic and flour and cook 1 minute. Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits, letting it bubble 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the broth, thyme and bay leaf, bring to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes. Remove the herbs and season with pepper and more salt.
Meanwhile toast the baguette slices on a baking sheet under the broiler for 1 to 2 minutes per side until crisp.
Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls on a baking sheet, float two toasts in each and cover with the cheese. Broil 2 to 4 minutes until bubbling and browned, and warn everyone the bowls are hot.

recipes.title: Lentilles aux Saucisses (French Lentils with Sausage)
recipes.summary: Peppery green lentils simmered with carrots, celery and thyme, finished with a splash of vinegar and Dijon and served with browned sausages. Hearty bistro food on a budget.

ingredients.name: pork sausages
ingredients.note: Toulouse-style or mild Italian, about 4 to 6 links

ingredients.name: green lentils
ingredients.note: French Puy lentils if you can find them; rinsed

instructions: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Brown the sausages 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned all over, then move them to a plate (they will finish cooking later).
Add the onion, carrots and celery to the fat in the pot and cook 6 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the lentils, broth, thyme and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer and nestle in the sausages.
Cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape and most of the broth is absorbed; add a splash of water if it gets dry. The sausages should reach 160°F.
Remove the bay leaf and stir the mustard and vinegar into the lentils. Season with salt and plenty of pepper, scatter with parsley and serve with the sausages on top.

recipes.title: Khoresh Gheimeh (Persian Split Pea and Beef Stew)
recipes.summary: Tender beef and yellow split peas braised in a tangy tomato sauce with turmeric, cinnamon and dried lime, topped with crisp potato sticks and served over rice.

ingredients.name: dried limes
ingredients.note: find them at Persian or Middle Eastern grocers or online (limoo amani); pierce with a knife. Or use 3 tbsp lemon juice at the end

ingredients.name: saffron
ingredients.note: ground and bloomed in 2 tbsp hot water

ingredients.name: potato sticks
ingredients.note: store-bought shoestring potato sticks, for topping

instructions: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Cook the onions 10 minutes, stirring, until golden.
Raise the heat to medium-high, add the beef, turmeric and cinnamon and cook 5 minutes, turning, until the meat is no longer pink on the outside.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until it darkens slightly. Add the split peas, water, pierced dried limes, salt and pepper.

Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 75 to 90 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beef is tender and the split peas are soft but still whole. Add a little water if the stew gets too thick.
Stir in the saffron water if using, and the lemon juice if you're not using dried limes. Taste for salt and tartness; press the limes against the pot to release more sourness if you like.
Serve over rice, topped with a handful of potato sticks just before eating so they stay crisp.

recipes.title: Kuku Sabzi (Persian Herb Frittata)
recipes.summary: A vivid green, oven-baked frittata packed with parsley, cilantro, dill and green onions, studded with walnuts. Eaten warm or cold with yogurt and flatbread.

ingredients.name: parsley
ingredients.note: leaves and tender stems, finely chopped

ingredients.name: cilantro
ingredients.note: leaves and tender stems, finely chopped

ingredients.name: dried barberries
ingredients.note: find them at Persian grocers or online; or chopped dried cranberries

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Wash and thoroughly dry the herbs (a salad spinner helps), then chop them very finely; a food processor in short pulses works too.
Whisk the eggs in a large bowl with the turmeric, baking powder, salt and pepper until frothy.
Stir in the herbs, green onions, walnuts and barberries. The mixture should look like mostly herbs held together with egg.
Pour the oil into a 10-inch oven-safe nonstick or cast-iron skillet and heat over medium until shimmering. Add the herb mixture, smooth the top and cook 4 to 5 minutes until the edges set.
Move the skillet to the oven and bake 18 to 20 minutes, until the center is firm when pressed and the top no longer looks wet.
Loosen the edges, slide onto a board and cut into wedges. Serve warm or at room temperature with plain yogurt, flatbread and sliced cucumber or radishes.

recipes.title: Joojeh Kabab (Persian Saffron Chicken Kebabs)
recipes.summary: Chicken thighs marinated in yogurt, grated onion, lemon and saffron, then grilled or broiled with tomatoes until juicy and charred at the edges.

ingredients.name: saffron
ingredients.note: about 1/4 tsp threads, ground and bloomed in 3 tbsp hot water; find it in the spice aisle or at Middle Eastern grocers. A pinch of turmeric gives the color, not the flavor

instructions: Grind the saffron threads with a pinch of salt using the back of a spoon, then stir in the hot water and let it steep 10 minutes until deep orange.
In a large bowl mix the grated onion, yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, pepper and two-thirds of the saffron water. Add the chicken and turn to coat.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour and up to overnight; the longer it sits the more tender and golden it gets.
Heat a grill to medium-high (or the broiler with a rack 5 inches from the heat). Thread the chicken onto skewers, wiping off excess marinade, and thread the tomatoes onto separate skewers.
Grill or broil 10 to 14 minutes, turning every few minutes, until the chicken is charred at the edges and reaches 175°F. Cook the tomatoes until blistered.
Stir the melted butter into the remaining saffron water and brush over the kebabs. Serve with saffron rice or flatbread, the tomatoes and a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.title: Chelow ba Tahdig (Persian Saffron Rice with Crispy Potato Crust)
recipes.summary: Fluffy steamed basmati crowned with saffron, made over a layer of potato slices that turn into a golden, crackly tahdig everyone will fight over.

ingredients.name: basmati rice
ingredients.note: rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.name: saffron
ingredients.note: about 1/4 tsp threads, ground and bloomed in 3 tbsp hot water; find it in the spice aisle or at Middle Eastern grocers

instructions: Bring the water and salt to a rolling boil in a large pot. Add the rinsed rice and boil 6 to 7 minutes, until the grains are soft outside but still have a firm bite in the center. Drain in a sieve and rinse briefly with lukewarm water.
In a 10-inch nonstick pot, heat the oil and 1 tbsp of the butter over medium heat with 1 tbsp of the saffron water. Lay the potato slices in a single snug layer over the bottom.
Spoon the rice over the potatoes, mounding it into a loose pyramid without packing it down. Poke 5 or 6 holes to the bottom with the handle of a wooden spoon.

Dot the rest of the butter over the rice. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel (tie the corners up away from the flame), cover tightly and cook on medium for 8 to 10 minutes, until you hear steady sizzling and see steam.
Turn the heat to low and steam 35 to 40 minutes, until the rice is fluffy and the potatoes are deep golden; peek at the edge with a spatula.

Spoon a cup of rice into a bowl, mix with the remaining saffron water and scatter it over the platter of rice. Loosen the tahdig, then flip the pot onto a plate or lift out the crispy potatoes, and serve with stews or kebabs.

recipes.title: Ash Reshteh (Persian Bean, Herb and Noodle Soup)
recipes.summary: A thick, herb-packed soup of beans, lentils and noodles, finished with tangy whey or sour cream, fried onions and mint oil. A simplified version for a home kitchen.

ingredients.name: linguine
ingredients.note: broken in half; or reshteh noodles from Persian grocers

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.note: thinned with a splash of water; or kashk (fermented whey) from Persian grocers

instructions: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Fry the onions 15 minutes, stirring, until deep golden. Scoop out half and set aside for topping.
Add the garlic and turmeric to the pot and stir 1 minute. Add the lentils and broth, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 20 minutes until the lentils are nearly tender.
Stir in the chickpeas, kidney beans, spinach, parsley, cilantro, dill, salt and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes until the greens are dark and soft.
Add the linguine and simmer 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't stick, until the noodles are tender and the soup is thick. Add water if it gets too thick to ladle.
Meanwhile warm the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a small pan over low heat, take it off the heat and stir in the dried mint for a few seconds until fragrant.
Stir a few spoonfuls of the thinned sour cream into the pot. Ladle into bowls and top with more sour cream, the fried onions and a drizzle of mint oil.

recipes.title: Salad-e Shirazi (Persian Cucumber, Tomato and Onion Salad)
recipes.summary: Finely diced cucumber, tomato and red onion tossed with lime juice and dried mint. Crisp, tangy and cooling next to rice, stews and kebabs.

ingredients.name: persian cucumbers
ingredients.note: or 1 English cucumber, cut into 1/4-inch dice

instructions: Dice the cucumbers, tomatoes and onion as small and evenly as you can; the fine dice is what makes this salad.
Put everything in a bowl with the lime juice, oil, dried mint (rubbed between your palms), salt and pepper.
Toss well and let it sit 5 to 10 minutes so the flavors meld. Taste and add more lime or salt, then serve cold, spooning up the juices over rice.

recipes.title: Menemen (Turkish Scrambled Eggs with Tomatoes and Peppers)
recipes.summary: Soft eggs stirred through sweet peppers and juicy tomatoes cooked down in olive oil. Mild, with a gentle warmth from Turkish pepper flakes that you can leave out.

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: finely chopped (optional in many Turkish homes)

ingredients.name: green bell pepper
ingredients.note: or Cubanelle or Anaheim peppers, chopped

ingredients.name: aleppo pepper
ingredients.note: pul biber; find it at Middle Eastern grocers or online, or use a pinch of red pepper flakes

instructions: Heat the oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and peppers 5 to 6 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the juices have mostly cooked off and the mixture looks jammy.
Lower the heat to medium-low. Crack in the eggs, wait 30 seconds, then gently stir and fold just until the eggs are softly set but still glossy, 2 to 3 minutes.
Take it off the heat, scatter with pepper flakes, feta and parsley, and serve straight from the pan with crusty bread for dipping.

recipes.title: Mercimek Çorbası (Turkish Red Lentil Soup)
recipes.summary: Red lentils simmered with onion, carrot and cumin, blended silky and finished with a squeeze of lemon. Gentle, cheap and soothing on a cold night.

ingredients.name: aleppo pepper
ingredients.note: pul biber or paprika, sizzled in a little butter, for topping

instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot 5 to 6 minutes until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and cumin and cook 1 minute until fragrant and brick red.
Add the lentils, broth and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils have completely broken down and the carrot is soft.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender (or carefully in batches). Thin with water if needed; it should be pourable like heavy cream. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls, drizzle with the pepper butter, sprinkle with dried mint and serve with lemon wedges to squeeze in at the table.

recipes.title: Çılbır (Turkish Poached Eggs with Garlic Yogurt)
recipes.summary: Soft poached eggs on cool garlicky yogurt, drizzled with warm butter sizzled with paprika and Aleppo pepper. Mild warmth; use sweet paprika only for no heat.

ingredients.name: aleppo pepper
ingredients.note: pul biber; find it at Middle Eastern grocers or online, or use 1/2 tsp paprika plus a pinch of red pepper flakes

instructions: Stir the yogurt with the garlic and salt and spread it over two shallow plates.

Bring a wide saucepan of water to a bare simmer and add the vinegar. Crack each egg into a small cup, swirl the water and slip the eggs in one or two at a time. Poach 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft, then lift out with a slotted spoon onto a paper towel.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat until foaming and lightly nutty, about 2 minutes. Take it off the heat and stir in the Aleppo pepper and paprika; it will turn a deep red.
Set two eggs on each plate of yogurt, spoon over the spiced butter, scatter with dill and serve right away with toasted bread.

recipes.title: İmam Bayıldı (Turkish Stuffed Eggplant with Tomatoes and Onions)
recipes.summary: Roasted eggplant halves filled with a sweet, garlicky tomato and onion stew, then baked in olive oil until meltingly soft. Best served warm or at room temperature.

ingredients.name: eggplants
ingredients.note: medium, about 1 lb each, halved lengthwise

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Score the cut sides of the eggplants in a crisscross without piercing the skin, brush with 2 tbsp of the oil, sprinkle with 1/2 tsp salt and roast cut side down on a lined sheet for 25 minutes until soft and browned underneath. (Traditionally they're fried; roasting is easier.)
Meanwhile heat 3 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions 10 minutes until soft and lightly golden, then add the garlic and pepper for 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar and the remaining 1 tsp salt and cook 8 minutes until thick and saucy. Stir in most of the parsley.
Turn the eggplants cut side up in a baking dish and press the flesh down with a spoon to make a deep hollow in each. Pile in the filling.
Pour the water and the last of the oil around the eggplants, cover with foil and bake at 375°F for 25 to 30 minutes until the eggplant collapses when pressed.
Drizzle with lemon juice and scatter with the remaining parsley. Let cool at least 10 minutes and serve warm or at room temperature with bread, rice or yogurt.

recipes.title: Izgara Köfte (Turkish Grilled Meatballs)
recipes.summary: Juicy oval beef patties seasoned with grated onion, cumin, paprika and parsley, cooked fast on a grill or in a skillet. Serve with flatbread, sliced onions and tomatoes.

ingredients.name: aleppo pepper
ingredients.note: pul biber; or a pinch of red pepper flakes

instructions: Put the beef, onion, garlic, breadcrumbs, parsley, cumin, paprika, salt, pepper and Aleppo pepper in a bowl. Knead with your hands for 2 to 3 minutes until the mixture turns sticky and holds together.
With wet hands, shape into 16 oval patties about 3 inches long and 1/2 inch thick. Chill 15 minutes if you have time; they hold their shape better.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and oil the grates (or heat a little oil in a large skillet).
Cook the köfte 4 to 5 minutes per side, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked through to 160°F.
Serve hot with warm flatbread, sliced tomatoes, thinly sliced onion tossed with parsley, and plain yogurt if you like.

recipes.title: Kısır (Turkish Bulgur Salad)
recipes.summary: Fine bulgur soaked in hot water, then tossed with tomato and pepper paste, herbs, cucumber and pomegranate molasses. Tangy, a little sweet and great for lunchboxes.

ingredients.name: fine bulgur
ingredients.note: #1 fine grind; find it at Middle Eastern grocers, or use medium bulgur soaked 10 minutes longer

ingredients.name: red pepper paste
ingredients.note: biber salçası; find it at Turkish grocers or online, or use 1 more tbsp tomato paste plus a pinch of red pepper flakes

ingredients.name: pomegranate molasses
ingredients.note: find it at Middle Eastern grocers or online; or 1 more tbsp lemon juice plus 1 tsp honey

instructions: Put the bulgur in a large bowl, pour over the boiling water, cover with a plate and let it stand 15 minutes until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.
While it's still warm, add the tomato paste, pepper paste, olive oil, lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, cumin and salt. Mix and rub with your hands or a spoon until every grain is evenly red.
Let it cool for 5 minutes, then fold in the green onions, parsley, mint, cucumber and tomatoes.
Taste and add more lemon, molasses or salt so it's bright and tangy. Serve at room temperature or chilled, with lettuce leaves for scooping.

recipes.title: Feijoada (Brazilian Black Bean and Pork Stew)
recipes.summary: A weeknight-friendly take on Brazil's beloved Saturday stew: black beans simmered with smoky sausage, bacon and tender pork until thick and rich. Serve with rice and orange slices.

ingredients.name: smoked sausage
ingredients.note: Portuguese linguiça or kielbasa, sliced into coins

instructions: Cook the bacon in a large Dutch oven over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes until crisp and the fat has rendered. Lift it out with a slotted spoon.
Season the pork cubes with salt and pepper and brown them in the bacon fat over medium-high heat, about 6 minutes, until deeply golden on a couple of sides. Add the sausage and brown 3 minutes more.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the black beans with their liquid, the broth, bay leaves and cooked bacon. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pork is tender.
Scoop out about 1 cup of beans, mash them with a fork and stir them back in. Simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes until the stew is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Discard the bay leaves and season to taste. Serve over white rice with orange slices and green onions on the side.

recipes.title: Moqueca (Brazilian Coconut Fish Stew)
recipes.summary: Bahian-style fish stew with peppers, tomato and coconut milk, brightened with lime and cilantro. Mild, golden and fragrant; lovely over rice.

ingredients.name: palm oil
ingredients.note: dendê; find it at Brazilian or West African grocers or online; or skip and add 1 tsp paprika

instructions: Toss the fish with the juice of 1 lime, the garlic and 1/2 tsp salt and let it sit for 15 minutes while you slice the vegetables.
Heat the olive oil in a wide, deep pan over medium heat. Add the onion and both peppers and cook 5 minutes until just softened, then stir in the paprika.
Lay the tomato slices over the vegetables, nestle the fish pieces on top in a single layer and spoon over any marinade.

Pour the coconut milk evenly over everything and drizzle with the palm oil if using. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook 12 to 15 minutes, without stirring, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Squeeze over the remaining lime, season with salt, scatter with cilantro and serve with white rice.

recipes.title: Strogonoff de Frango (Brazilian Chicken Stroganoff)
recipes.summary: Brazil's favorite family stroganoff: tender chicken in a creamy, slightly sweet tomato sauce with mushrooms. Served with rice and crunchy potato sticks.
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken 5 to 6 minutes, stirring once or twice, until lightly golden.
Add the onion and mushrooms and cook 5 minutes until the mushrooms release their liquid and it mostly evaporates. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the ketchup and mustard and cook 1 minute until they coat everything and turn a shade darker.
Lower the heat to medium-low, pour in the cream and simmer gently 4 to 5 minutes until the sauce is pale pink and lightly thickened and the chicken is cooked through. Don't let it boil hard.
Taste for salt and serve over white rice with a handful of potato sticks on top for crunch.

recipes.title: Pão de Queijo (Brazilian Cheese Bread)
recipes.summary: Crisp-shelled, chewy little cheese puffs made with tapioca flour, so they're naturally gluten-free. Great warm from the oven as a snack or with dinner.

ingredients.name: tapioca starch
ingredients.note: also sold as tapioca flour, in the baking or gluten-free aisle

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Put the tapioca starch in a large bowl.
Bring the milk, oil and salt just to a boil in a small saucepan, then pour it over the tapioca starch and stir hard with a wooden spoon until it forms a sticky, lumpy dough. Let it cool 10 minutes.
Add the eggs a little at a time, beating well after each addition, until the dough is smooth and stretchy. Mix in the cheese.
With oiled hands, roll the dough into 1 1/2-inch balls and set them 2 inches apart on the baking sheet.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and pale golden with a few browned spots. Serve warm. Unbaked balls freeze well; bake from frozen for a few extra minutes.

recipes.title: Picanha-Style Steak with Farofa
recipes.summary: Churrasco at home: a thick, fat-capped sirloin grilled with coarse salt, sliced thin and served with farofa, a buttery toasted cassava crumb with bacon and onion.

ingredients.name: sirloin steak
ingredients.note: top sirloin cap (picanha) with its fat cap, or thick-cut top sirloin

ingredients.name: cassava meal
ingredients.note: farinha de mandioca; find it at Brazilian or Latin grocers or online; or use supermarket cassava flour

instructions: Heat a grill to medium-high. Score the fat cap of the steak in a shallow crosshatch without cutting into the meat, then rub all over with the coarse salt and let it sit while the grill heats.
For the farofa, cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat 5 minutes until crisp. Add the butter and onion and cook 4 minutes until golden, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the cassava meal and stir constantly 4 to 5 minutes until it smells toasty and turns sandy-golden. Season with pepper, stir in the parsley and set aside.
Grill the steak fat side down for 4 to 5 minutes until the fat is crisp and browned, watching for flare-ups. Flip and grill 5 to 7 minutes per side for medium-rare, about 130°F inside.
Rest the steak 5 to 10 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain and serve with the farofa sprinkled alongside. A bowl of vinagrete is the classic partner.

recipes.title: Vinagrete (Brazilian Tomato and Onion Salsa)
recipes.summary: The fresh, tangy salsa that sits next to every Brazilian barbecue: diced tomato, onion and pepper in a light vinegar dressing. Spoon it over steak, beans or rice.
instructions: Put the diced onion in a sieve and rinse it under cold water for a few seconds to soften its bite, then shake dry.
Combine the tomatoes, onion, green pepper and parsley in a bowl.
Whisk the vinegar, olive oil, water and salt together, pour over the vegetables and toss well.
Let it stand at least 10 minutes so the flavors mingle, then taste for salt. It keeps covered in the fridge for a day.

recipes.title: Lomo Saltado (Peruvian Beef and Potato Stir-Fry)
recipes.summary: Peru's famous Chinese-Peruvian stir-fry: seared beef strips, red onion and tomato tossed in a soy-vinegar sauce with crisp fries. Mild unless you add the ají amarillo.

ingredients.name: ají amarillo chili paste
ingredients.note: find it at Latin American grocers or online (jarred, often Goya or Inca's Food); or blend 1 roasted yellow bell pepper with 1 seeded jalapeño per 3 tbsp

instructions: Bake the fries according to the package until crisp, usually 20 to 25 minutes, so they're ready when the stir-fry is.
Meanwhile, toss the beef with the garlic, cumin, 1 tbsp soy sauce, salt and pepper. Mix the remaining soy sauce with the vinegar and the ají amarillo paste if using.

Heat a large skillet or wok over high heat until smoking. Add 1 tbsp oil and half the beef in a single layer and sear 2 minutes without moving, then toss 1 minute until browned. Repeat with the rest of the beef.
Add the remaining oil, the onion wedges and cook 2 minutes until charred at the edges but still crunchy. Add the tomatoes and cook 1 minute, just until they start to soften.
Return the beef, pour in the soy-vinegar mixture and toss 1 minute until glossy. Fold in the hot fries and cilantro and serve right away with white rice.

recipes.title: Ají de Gallina (Peruvian Creamy Chicken in Yellow Pepper Sauce)
recipes.summary: Shredded chicken in a velvety sauce of ají amarillo, bread, milk, walnuts and cheese, served over potatoes and rice. Gently warm and fruity, not fiery; use less paste for milder.

ingredients.name: ají amarillo chili paste
ingredients.note: find it at Latin American grocers or online (jarred, often Goya or Inca's Food); or blend 1 roasted yellow bell pepper with 1 seeded jalapeño per 3 tbsp

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: Yukon Gold, boiled and halved, to serve

ingredients.name: black olives
ingredients.note: Kalamata or Peruvian botija, to serve

instructions: Put the chicken in a pot with the broth, bring to a simmer and cook covered on low 15 to 18 minutes until cooked through. Lift out the chicken, keep the broth, and shred the meat with two forks.
Tear the bread into a blender, pour over the evaporated milk and let it soak 5 minutes. Add the walnuts and blend until completely smooth.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 6 to 8 minutes until soft and golden, then stir in the garlic, ají amarillo paste and turmeric for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the bread mixture and 1 cup of the reserved broth and simmer, stirring often, 5 minutes until it thickens to a creamy sauce. Add more broth if it gets too stiff.
Stir in the shredded chicken and parmesan and heat through 3 minutes. Season with salt.
Spoon over the boiled potatoes and serve with rice, topped with egg quarters and olives.

recipes.title: Pollo a la Brasa (Peruvian Roast Chicken) with Ají Verde
recipes.summary: Oven-roasted take on Peru's rotisserie chicken, rubbed with garlic, cumin, lime and soy, plus a bright green jalapeño-cilantro sauce. The sauce is medium-hot; seed the jalapeños for milder.

ingredients.name: chicken leg quarters
ingredients.note: about 4, or bone-in thighs and drumsticks

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: 6 grated for the rub, 1 for the sauce

instructions: Mix the soy sauce, juice of 2 limes, 6 grated garlic cloves, cumin, paprika, oregano, oil and pepper. Rub it all over the chicken and under the skin. Marinate at least 15 minutes, or covered in the fridge overnight.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Arrange the chicken skin side up on a foil-lined sheet pan, spooning any marinade over the top.
Roast 40 to 45 minutes until the skin is deep mahogany and crisp and the thickest part reads 175°F. If the skin darkens too fast, tent loosely with foil.
Meanwhile, blend the cilantro, jalapeños, mayonnaise, parmesan, remaining garlic clove and juice of the last lime until smooth and bright green. Season with salt and chill until serving.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then serve with the ají verde for dipping, plus fries or rice and a simple salad.

recipes.title: Causa Limeña (Peruvian Layered Potato Terrine)
recipes.summary: Chilled layers of silky lime-and-ají mashed potato with avocado and an egg-mayo filling. A cool, colorful starter or light lunch; mild, with gentle pepper warmth.

ingredients.name: ají amarillo chili paste
ingredients.note: find it at Latin American grocers or online (jarred, often Goya or Inca's Food); or blend 1 roasted yellow bell pepper with 1 seeded jalapeño per 3 tbsp

instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water 15 to 20 minutes until completely tender when pierced. Drain well and let them steam dry for 5 minutes.

Press the potatoes through a ricer or mash until perfectly smooth. While still warm, beat in the ají amarillo paste, lime juice, oil and salt until it forms a smooth, yellow dough. Let it cool completely.
Chop 2 of the eggs and mix with the mayonnaise, red onion and a pinch of salt. Squeeze a little lime over the avocado slices so they stay green.

Line an 8-inch loaf pan or square dish with plastic wrap. Press in half the potato in an even layer, top with the avocado, then the egg salad, and finish with the rest of the potato, smoothing the top.
Chill at least 30 minutes until firm. Turn out onto a plate, slice and garnish with the remaining egg and the olives.

recipes.title: Papa a la Huancaína (Potatoes in Creamy Ají Cheese Sauce)
recipes.summary: Sliced potatoes draped in a smooth, golden sauce of ají amarillo, fresh cheese and milk, served cool over lettuce. Mildly warm; reduce the paste for little ones.

ingredients.name: evaporated milk
ingredients.note: plus a splash more if needed

ingredients.name: ají amarillo chili paste
ingredients.note: find it at Latin American grocers or online (jarred, often Goya or Inca's Food); or blend 1 roasted yellow bell pepper with 1 seeded jalapeño per 3 tbsp

instructions: Boil the whole potatoes in salted water 18 to 20 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain, cool slightly, then peel and slice into thick rounds.
Meanwhile, warm 1 tbsp oil in a small skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and garlic 3 minutes until soft but not browned. Stir in the ají amarillo paste for 1 minute.

Scrape the onion mixture into a blender with the queso fresco, evaporated milk and remaining oil. Blend until silky and the thickness of heavy cream; add a splash more milk if too thick, or a little more cheese if too thin. Season with salt.
Line a platter with lettuce leaves, lay the potato slices on top and pour the sauce over generously.
Garnish with the egg halves and olives and serve at room temperature or lightly chilled.

recipes.title: Sopa de Quinua (Peruvian Quinoa and Vegetable Soup)
recipes.summary: A gentle Andean soup of quinoa, potato and carrot in a light broth with oregano and fresh cilantro. Simple, filling and easy to make on a busy night.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes until soft and translucent, then stir in the garlic and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed quinoa and stir 1 minute to toast it lightly.
Pour in the broth, add the potatoes and carrots and bring to a boil. Lower the heat and simmer 20 minutes, partly covered, until the potatoes are tender and the quinoa shows its little white curls.
Season with salt and stir in the cilantro. The soup thickens as it sits; loosen leftovers with a splash of broth or water when reheating.

recipes.title: Nigerian Jollof Rice
recipes.summary: Party-style jollof: rice simmered in a smoky blended pepper and tomato sauce until every grain is red. Medium heat from Scotch bonnet; use half or skip it for kids.

ingredients.name: yellow onion
ingredients.note: 1 roughly chopped for blending, 1 thinly sliced

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: find it at Caribbean or African grocers, or some supermarkets; or use 1 habanero, or 1 jalapeño for much milder

ingredients.name: curry powder
ingredients.note: a mild, Caribbean- or Nigerian-style curry powder if you have it

ingredients.name: long-grain rice
ingredients.note: parboiled rice is traditional; rinse until the water runs clear

ingredients.name: vegetable broth
ingredients.note: use chicken broth if you don't need it vegetarian
