instructions: Blend the bell peppers, tomatoes, chopped onion, Scotch bonnet, garlic and ginger until smooth. Simmer this pepper base in a saucepan over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens and loses its raw smell.
Heat the oil in a heavy Dutch oven over medium heat. Fry the sliced onion for 4 minutes until soft, then stir in the tomato paste and fry it for 3 to 4 minutes until it darkens to a brick red.
Add the reduced pepper base, curry powder, thyme, bay leaves and salt. Fry the sauce for 5 minutes, stirring, until oil starts to pool on the surface.
Stir in the rinsed rice and broth, bring to a boil, then turn the heat to the lowest setting. Cover with a sheet of foil and then the lid to trap the steam.

Cook for 25 to 30 minutes without stirring, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. If the rice is still firm, sprinkle in 1/4 cup water and cook 5 minutes more; a little toasty crust on the bottom is prized.
Remove the bay leaves, fluff with a fork and adjust the salt. Serve with fried plantains, chicken or a simple salad.

recipes.title: Groundnut Stew with Chicken and Sweet Potatoes
recipes.summary: West African peanut stew: chicken and sweet potato simmered in a rich tomato and peanut sauce with spinach. Mild to medium heat; drop the Scotch bonnet for kids.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.note: boneless, skinless, cut into large chunks

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes (about 1 1/2 lb)

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: left whole and pricked for gentle heat; find it at Caribbean or African grocers, or some supermarkets; or use 1 habanero, or 1 jalapeño for much milder

instructions: Season the chicken with 1 tsp salt. Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the chicken in two batches, about 4 minutes per batch, then set aside.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, ginger, smoked paprika and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until the paste darkens.
Add the tomatoes and broth, then whisk in the peanut butter until smooth. Return the chicken, add the sweet potatoes and drop in the whole pricked Scotch bonnet.
Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often so the peanut sauce doesn't catch, until the sweet potatoes are tender and the sauce coats a spoon.
Fish out the Scotch bonnet (or mash it into the stew for more heat). Stir in the spinach until wilted and season with salt.
Serve over rice or with fufu, sprinkled with chopped peanuts.

recipes.title: Chicken Yassa (Senegalese Lemon-Onion Chicken)
recipes.summary: Senegal's beloved yassa: lemon-and-mustard marinated chicken browned, then braised in a mountain of soft, tangy onions. Gentle warmth; the chili is optional.

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: left whole for a hint of heat; find it at Caribbean or African grocers, or some supermarkets; or use 1 habanero, or 1 jalapeño for much milder

instructions: Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt, pepper and 1 tbsp oil in a large bowl. Add the chicken and sliced onions and toss well; marinate at least 15 minutes, or covered in the fridge up to overnight.

Lift the chicken out of the marinade and pat dry, keeping the onions and liquid. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the chicken skin side down for 6 to 7 minutes until deep golden, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil and the onions (shake off the marinade, but keep it). Cook over medium heat, stirring often, for 15 minutes until the onions are soft, sweet and light golden.
Pour in the reserved marinade and broth, add the bay leaves and the whole Scotch bonnet if using, and nestle the chicken back in skin side up.
Cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes, adding the olives for the last 5 minutes, until the chicken is tender and at least 175°F near the bone.
Taste the onion sauce and adjust with salt or a squeeze more lemon, then serve over white rice.

recipes.title: Red-Red (Ghanaian Black-Eyed Pea Stew with Baked Plantains)
recipes.summary: Ghana's red-red: black-eyed peas in a rich tomato and palm oil sauce, served with sweet oven-baked plantains instead of fried. Mild-medium heat; skip the chili for kids.

ingredients.name: ripe plantains
ingredients.note: yellow with plenty of black spots

ingredients.name: red palm oil
ingredients.note: find it at African or Latin grocers or online; or use vegetable oil plus 1/2 tsp sweet paprika for color

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: minced, seeds removed; find it at Caribbean or African grocers, or some supermarkets; or use 1 habanero, or 1 jalapeño for much milder

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment. Peel the plantains, slice on the diagonal 1/2 inch thick, toss with the vegetable oil and a pinch of salt, and spread out in one layer.
Bake the plantains for 20 to 25 minutes, flipping halfway, until caramelized and dark golden at the edges.
Meanwhile, warm the palm oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, ginger and Scotch bonnet and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and smoked paprika and fry for 2 minutes until brick red, then add the diced tomatoes and simmer 6 to 8 minutes until thick and jammy.
Add the black-eyed peas and water, simmer 10 minutes, and lightly mash a few peas against the pan to thicken the sauce. Season with salt.
Serve the stew with the baked plantains alongside. Traditionally it is topped with gari (toasted cassava), if you can find it.

recipes.title: Suya-Spiced Chicken Skewers
recipes.summary: Nigerian street-food suya flavors on chicken: a peanut, ginger and cayenne rub, grilled until charred and served with sliced onion and tomato. Fairly hot; halve the cayenne for milder.

ingredients.name: roasted peanuts
ingredients.note: unsalted, finely ground in a food processor (stop before it turns to butter)

instructions: If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 15 minutes. Mix the ground peanuts, paprika, cayenne, ginger, garlic powder, onion powder and crumbled bouillon cube to make the yaji (suya spice).
Toss the chicken with the oil, then with about two-thirds of the spice mix until well coated. Thread onto skewers, leaving small gaps between pieces.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and oil the grates. Grill the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until charred in spots and the chicken reaches 165°F.
Sprinkle the hot skewers with a little more of the remaining spice mix, keeping some at the table for anyone who wants more heat.
Pile onto a platter with the red onion, tomatoes and cucumber, and squeeze lime over just before serving.

recipes.title: Efo Riro with Shrimp (Nigerian Spinach Stew)
recipes.summary: A Yoruba-style spinach stew: spinach folded into a fried red pepper sauce with shrimp. Made approachable with frozen spinach. Medium-hot; use half the Scotch bonnet for milder.

ingredients.name: yellow onion
ingredients.note: half roughly chopped for blending, half thinly sliced

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: find it at Caribbean or African grocers, or some supermarkets; or use 1 habanero, or 1 jalapeño for much milder

ingredients.name: red palm oil
ingredients.note: find it at African or Latin grocers or online; or use vegetable oil plus 1/2 tsp sweet paprika for color

ingredients.name: frozen chopped spinach
ingredients.note: thawed and squeezed very dry; or 2 lb fresh spinach, blanched and squeezed

ingredients.name: smoked paprika
ingredients.note: stands in for the smoky depth of dried fish

ingredients.name: ground crayfish
ingredients.note: find it at African grocers or online; skip if you can't find it

instructions: Blend the bell peppers, tomatoes, the chopped half onion and the Scotch bonnet until fairly smooth. Simmer in a saucepan over medium heat for 10 minutes until reduced and thick.
Warm the palm oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and garlic and cook 3 to 4 minutes until soft and fragrant.
Add the reduced pepper sauce, bouillon cube, smoked paprika and crayfish if using. Fry for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the sauce darkens and the oil rises to the top.
Add the shrimp and cook 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until just pink.
Stir in the squeezed spinach, cover and cook 3 to 4 minutes until heated through; don't overcook or the spinach turns drab. Season with salt and serve with rice, pounded yam or fufu.

recipes.title: Chicken Karahi
recipes.summary: Lahore-style karahi: chicken cooked fast and hot with tomatoes, ginger, garlic, black pepper and green chilies until the sauce clings. Medium-hot; use 1 seeded chili for milder.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.note: boneless or bone-in, cut into 2-inch pieces

ingredients.name: ginger
ingredients.note: half grated, half cut into thin matchsticks for garnish

ingredients.name: serrano peppers
ingredients.note: slit lengthwise; use 1, seeded, for milder

ingredients.name: kashmiri chili powder
ingredients.note: or 1/2 tsp paprika plus 1/4 tsp cayenne

instructions: Heat the oil in a wok, karahi or wide skillet over high heat. Add the chicken and fry for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until it loses its pink color and starts to brown at the edges.
Add the garlic and grated ginger and stir-fry 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and salt, cover, and cook on medium-high for 8 minutes until the tomatoes collapse.
Uncover and use a spoon to pick out and discard any loose tomato skins if you like. Stir in the chili powder, coriander, cumin and black pepper.
Keep cooking uncovered on high, stirring and scraping, for 8 to 10 minutes until the sauce thickens, the oil separates around the edges and the chicken is cooked through.
Lower the heat, stir in the yogurt and slit serranos and cook 2 minutes more. Add the ghee if using, sprinkle with garam masala, ginger matchsticks and cilantro, and serve with naan or roti.

recipes.title: Daal Chawal (Chana Daal with Cumin Rice)
recipes.summary: Pakistan's everyday comfort plate: creamy split chickpea daal finished with a sizzling garlic and red chili tarka, over cumin rice. Mild-medium; skip the dried chilies for kids.

ingredients.name: chana dal
ingredients.note: find it at South Asian grocers; or use yellow split peas (cook 10 to 15 minutes longer)

ingredients.name: chili powder
ingredients.note: use kashmiri chili powder or paprika for milder

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or ghee, if you don't need it vegan

instructions: Rinse the chana dal and soak it in hot water while you prep, about 10 minutes. Drain, then simmer with 4 cups water, the turmeric, chili powder and 1 tsp salt, partly covered, for 40 to 45 minutes until the dal is soft and breaks when pressed; add more water if it gets too thick.
Meanwhile, put the rice, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp salt and 2 1/4 cups water in a pot. Bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Whisk or mash the cooked dal lightly so it turns creamy but still has some texture. Stir in the chopped tomato and simmer 5 minutes.

For the tarka, heat the oil in a small skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the onion for 6 to 8 minutes until deep golden, then add the remaining cumin, the garlic and dried chilies and cook 30 to 60 seconds until the garlic is light golden.
Pour the sizzling tarka over the dal, scatter with cilantro and serve over the cumin rice with lemon wedges and a simple salad or achar on the side.

recipes.title: Aloo Keema (Spiced Ground Beef with Potatoes)
recipes.summary: A Pakistani home-cooking staple: ground beef simmered with onions, tomatoes, warm spices, potatoes and peas. Mild-medium; leave out the green chili for kids.

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: Yukon Gold, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes

instructions: Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion for 6 to 7 minutes until golden at the edges.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute, then add the beef and break it up with a spoon. Cook 5 to 6 minutes until no pink remains.
Stir in the tomatoes, salt, cumin, coriander, turmeric and chili powder. Cook 5 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes break down and the oil starts to separate from the meat.
Add the potatoes and water, cover and simmer on medium-low for 15 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the potatoes are tender when pierced.

Stir in the peas, garam masala and serrano if using, and cook uncovered 3 to 4 minutes until the peas are hot and the mixture is thick rather than soupy. Finish with cilantro and serve with roti, naan or rice.

recipes.title: Chana Pulao (Chickpea Rice with Whole Spices)
recipes.summary: Fragrant basmati cooked in a light onion stock with chickpeas and whole spices: a classic Pakistani one-pot rice. Gently spiced, not hot; serve with raita for dairy-eaters.

ingredients.name: basmati rice
ingredients.note: rinsed, then soaked 20 minutes and drained

ingredients.name: green cardamom pods
ingredients.note: lightly crushed; find them in the spice aisle or South Asian grocers

instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring, for 10 to 12 minutes until evenly deep golden brown; this color gives the pulao its flavor.
Add the cumin, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, peppercorns and bay leaves and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the garlic, ginger and tomato and cook 3 minutes until the tomato softens.
Add the chickpeas, broth and salt and bring to a rolling boil. Taste the liquid: it should be a little saltier than you'd like soup.
Gently stir in the drained rice, return to a boil and cook uncovered on medium-high for 3 to 4 minutes until the water drops just below the surface of the rice and little holes appear.
Cover tightly, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff gently with a fork, scatter with cilantro and serve with raita or a cucumber-tomato salad.

recipes.title: Weeknight Chicken Biryani
recipes.summary: A streamlined Pakistani-style chicken biryani: spiced yogurt chicken layered with par-boiled basmati, fried onions and mint, then steamed. Medium heat; use 1 chili for milder.

ingredients.name: biryani masala
ingredients.note: find it in the international aisle or South Asian grocers; or use 2 tbsp garam masala plus 1 tsp chili powder

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: divided, plus more for the rice water

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: small Yukon Gold, peeled and halved; a Karachi favorite

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.note: warmed, with a pinch of saffron or 2 drops yellow food coloring

instructions: Mix the chicken with the yogurt, biryani masala, garlic, ginger and 1 1/2 tsp salt and set aside while you fry the onions.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and fry the onions, stirring often, for 12 to 15 minutes until deep golden brown. Lift out half for layering.

Add the tomatoes and serranos to the pot and cook 4 minutes until soft. Add the chicken and its marinade and the potatoes if using, then cover and simmer on medium-low for 20 minutes, stirring once, until the chicken is cooked and the sauce is thick.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of water to a boil with 2 tbsp salt. Add the drained rice and boil for 5 to 6 minutes until it is about 70% cooked, still firm in the center, then drain.

Scatter half the mint, cilantro and reserved onions over the chicken, sprinkle with lemon juice, then spread the rice on top. Top with the remaining herbs and onions and drizzle over the saffron milk if using.

Cover tightly with foil and the lid and cook on the lowest heat for 15 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and steaming. Rest 5 minutes, then scoop from the bottom so everyone gets chicken and rice. Serve with raita.

recipes.title: Oven-Baked Seekh Kebabs
recipes.summary: Pakistani BBQ-style seekh kebabs, shaped on skewers and broiled: juicy ground beef with onion, ginger, green chili and herbs. Medium heat; seed the chilies for milder.

ingredients.name: serrano peppers
ingredients.note: finely minced; seed them for milder

instructions: Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches below it and line a sheet pan with foil. If using wooden skewers, soak 8 of them in water.

Put the beef, squeezed onion, garlic, ginger, serranos, cilantro, mint, cumin, coriander, garam masala, chili flakes and salt in a bowl. Knead firmly with your hands for 2 to 3 minutes until the mixture turns sticky; this keeps the kebabs on the skewers.
With wet hands, divide into 8 portions and squeeze each one into a long, even sausage around a skewer, about 1 inch thick. Chill 10 minutes if they feel soft.
Lay the skewers on the pan, brush with oil and broil for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every 4 minutes, until browned and charred in spots and 160°F inside.
Rest 2 minutes, then serve with onion rings, lemon wedges, naan and mint chutney or yogurt sauce.
